confirmed.title: Two registered descriptive route flags are never computed
confirmed.file_line: lcr/fixtures.py:1157-1160 (trigger() route dict); lcr/fixtures.py:1163-1184 (gate_from_results); lcr/fixtures.py:1253-1262 (FIXTURE_GATE.json body)
confirmed.rule_text: route_classification.descriptive_flags: ["d0_version_already_qualifies ...", "constrained_qualifies", "weighted_qualifies", "best constrained vs best weighted I12", "joint vs sequential I12"]
confirmed.code_behaviour: trigger() returns decoder_enabled, assignment_search_helps, best_fm_I12, best_new_I12 (weighted and constrained pooled), d0_version_already_qualifies, constrained_qualifies and weighted_qualifies. No code in lcr/ computes a best-constrained I12, a best-weighted I12 or any joint-versus-sequential I12 comparison (grep finds these strings only in the gate_rule() text). Neither flag is written to FIXTURE_GATE.json. The rule also never says which arms or set they cover: qualifying or all arms; W-JOINT vs W-SEQ-12/21 per lambda, K-JOINT-SINGLE/PAIR vs K-SEQ-12/21, or the d1_fixed JOINT vs SEQ maps.
confirmed.failure_scenario: On F4_REDUNDANT, whose stated purpose is that sequential and joint should not differ, and on F3_COMPLEMENTARY_XOR, the locked FIXTURE_GATE.json contains no joint-vs-sequential or constrained-vs-weighted value. Whoever writes FIXTURE_ORACLE_REPORT.md must then derive these two registered descriptive outputs after the fact from the per-arm I12 rows, choosing the arm set and the qualifying/all scope at that point. That is a post-hoc definition of a registered output. Verdict and route are unaffected.

verdict.reason:
The claim holds. FIXTURE_GATE_RULE.json route_classification.descriptive_flags (generated at lcr/fixtures.py:390-393) lists five descriptive outputs. trigger() (lcr/fixtures.py:1155-1160) computes only three of them in its route dict: d0_version_already_qualifies, constrained_qualifies and weighted_qualifies. Nothing computes "best constrained vs best weighted I12" or "joint vs sequential I12":
- In lcr/, those strings appear only in the gate_rule() text.
- gate_from_results (1163-1184) and the FIXTURE_GATE.json body (1253-1262) add nothing beyond trigger()'s route dict.
- The independent verifier does not compute them either. Its write_oracle_report (verification/replay_lcr.py:8659-8735) prints only T_star, qualifying, decoder_enabled, assignment_search_helps, best_fm_I12 and best_new_I12.

The raw material is in FIXTURE_GATE.json: per-arm I12, feasible and local_ok for every config id, under fixtures[].arms and trigger.qualifying/not_qualifying. So the values can be derived later. But the rule never says which set they cover (qualifying only, feasible+local_ok, or all arms). It also never says which comparisons count: W-JOINT vs W-SEQ-12/21 per lambda, K-JOINT-SINGLE/PAIR vs K-SEQ-12/21, d1_fixed JOINT vs SEQ, or how the two SEQ orders combine. Whoever writes the report would have to choose those definitions after seeing the results, for registered outputs. The prompt's fixture-gate section names these as "separate empirical component questions" and lists "both sequential orders; JOINT-SINGLE; JOINT-PAIR" as comparisons. F4 exists specifically as a joint-vs-sequential no-difference case. So the gap is real.

Verdict and route are unaffected: helps and route use only fm/new, best_fm and best_new. Severity is disclosure-only.
verdict.suggested_fix:
Define the two outputs before the lock and compute them in trigger() so they land in FIXTURE_GATE.json. Minimal code, in trigger() before the return, using the arms already in `arms` with eligibility E(c) = feasible and local_ok (report each value both over E and over `qual`):
- best_constrained_I12 = min I12 over constrained arms U|K-*|i8o64|D1. best_weighted_I12 = min I12 over U|W-*|i8o64|l*|D1. Report their difference (constrained minus weighted). Use None when a set is empty.
- joint_vs_seq:
  - Weighted, per lambda: I12(W-JOINT|l) - min(I12(W-SEQ-12|l), I12(W-SEQ-21|l)).
  - d1_fixed, per lambda: I12(JOINT|l|D1) - min(I12(SEQ-12|l|D1), I12(SEQ-21|l|D1)).
  - Constrained: min(I12 K-JOINT-SINGLE, K-JOINT-PAIR) - min(I12 K-SEQ-12, K-SEQ-21).
  - Each entry carries the eligibility of both sides.

Add these keys to the route dict under a "descriptive" sub-key and state the same definitions verbatim in gate_rule()'s descriptive_flags, marked "descriptive, never enters verdict/route; not required by the trigger (prompt section on the trigger)". If the study does not want them computed at the gate, the text-only alternative is to remove those two strings from descriptive_flags and say they are Adult component questions (claims B/C), not fixture-gate outputs.

confirmed.title: C5 never checks the mapper's incremental search terms: 'final_state_terms' is a fresh rebuild, so C5 compares two from-scratch computations
confirmed.rule_text: Prompt sec. 9, mandatory correctness: 'incremental MI/loss terms match independent reconstruction'. Registered C5: 'mapper final_state_terms and deployed terms (L1, L2, B1, B2, I1, I2, I12, T, Phi) equal the independent reconstruction within 1e-10'.
confirmed.code_behaviour: fit_unit throws away the winning search State. It builds a new State(pb_rec, final_labels) from the final labels (mapper.py:1250) and records that state's terms as final_state_terms. The incremental state is the one updated by apply/undo deltas to Tr, T12 and the memo-solved tll/tbr, and _winner (mapper.py:1227) uses it to rank candidates and decide feasibility. Its terms appear only in rec['starts'][k]['final']['terms'], and best[0] is never compared with objective(ft, w). fixtures.py C5 reads only rec['final_state_terms'] and rec['deployed']['terms']. Both are from-scratch values, the release and the oracle are from-scratch too, and nothing on the fixture runs touches the per-move deltas or the incrementally maintained tables. (lcr/tests/test_mapper.py has a synthetic incremental-vs-scratch unit test, but that is not part of the gate.)
confirmed.failure_scenario: Suppose State.apply/undo drifts the T12 or Tr table after recipient-2 moves, for example a wrong axis in grow(). W- and K- arms then rank and accept moves on wrong I12 or Phi values, and K- arms may judge feasibility on wrong values. The final labels are still rebuilt correctly, so final_state_terms, deployed terms and the oracle agree within 1e-12. C5 passes, C6 only labels the arms HEURISTIC, and the trigger runs on independent release metrics. The output is GATE_MET even though the prompt's mandatory incremental-terms check is false; it should be GATE_NOT_MET with CORRECTNESS_FAILURE:C5. Fix: in C5, compare each refined start's rec['starts'][..]['final']['terms'] (and the winner's search-state objective) with the reconstruction within 1e-10, and/or record and check the rejected_on_exact_recheck counts.

verdict.reason:
The claim holds; I checked the code myself. In fit_unit (lcr/mapper.py:1243-1251) the winning search State, cands[best[1]][2], is used only to take canonical_labels. A new State(pb_rec, final_labels) is then built from scratch, and its terms() become rec['final_state_terms'] (mapper.py:1317) and rec['winner']['objective']. The parity check at mapper.py:1270-1279 compares that rebuilt state (ft) with deployed_terms, which is also computed from scratch. The fixture gate's C5 check (lcr/fixtures.py:982-996) reads only rec['final_state_terms'] and rec['deployed']['terms']. The independent reconstruction (arms[cid]['metrics'], oracle tables) is from scratch as well. A grep shows fixtures.py never reads rec['starts'], never touches State or apply, and never compares best[0] or any start's 'final' terms.

The incrementally maintained search state is never compared with anything on the fixture runs. That state is what _accept, _pair_step, _winner and the K-arm feasibility tests use: Tr/T12 are updated by grow() deltas in State.apply/undo, and the per-move dL/dB/dI/dI12 deltas come from _cell. Its terms are stored only in rec['starts'][k]['final']['terms'], which the gate does not read. The only incremental-vs-scratch comparison is the synthetic unit test lcr/tests/test_mapper.py:89. It is not part of the gate, and the registered GATE_MET requires every mandatory check to pass on all four fixtures.

The prompt's binding list of mandatory correctness checks includes 'incremental MI/loss terms match independent reconstruction' (prompt line 315). C5 is the check that corresponds to that item. Its registered wording ('mapper final_state_terms ... equal the independent reconstruction') literally matches the code, but the field it names is a from-scratch rebuild. So the registered gate as written and coded does not check the prompt's mandatory incremental item.

Severity is conditional, not certain. The loss and Brier side (L/B) is largely guarded at runtime: State.apply calls ensure(verify=True) and refolds after each move, both requiring bitwise equality of (n, Y, S). The MI side has no runtime check at all: the incremental Tr/T12 tables, and from them I1, I2, I12 and Phi of the search state. Suppose grow(), apply() or undo() had a sign or axis error. W- and K- arms would then rank moves, and K- arms would screen feasibility, on wrong MI values. C5 would still pass, because the rebuilt and deployed values agree with the oracle. C6 would only label the arm HEURISTIC, and the trigger would read independent metrics. The gate could report GATE_MET even though the mandatory incremental check never ran. The K-arm deployed-feasibility assertion catches only the subcase where the wrong values make an infeasible release look feasible.
verdict.suggested_fix: This needs only a change in fixtures.py plus matching text; mapper.py is untouched. In lcr/fixtures.py C5 (after line 996), add a third block per mapper record: the winning candidate's incrementally maintained search-state terms. Find it as follows: wk = rec['winner']['kind']; wn = rec['winner']['start']. Pick sr = the entry of rec['starts'] whose name ((s.get('name') or s['start']['name'])) == wn. Then set t = sr['final']['terms'] if wk.startswith('refined'), t = sr['unchanged']['terms'] if wk == 'unchanged', and skip for 'unchanged_descriptive', which has no search state. Compare TERM_KEYS plus T and Phi (where present; C-TASK search has no SEX terms) with arms[cid]['metrics'] within TOL_TERMS, append failures as f'{cid}:search_state:{k}', and include them in max_abs_diff. Change the registered C5 text to: 'the winning candidate's incrementally maintained search-state terms (rec.starts[winner].final.terms), mapper final_state_terms (from-scratch rebuild) and deployed terms (L1, L2, B1, B2, I1, I2, I12, T, Phi) equal the independent reconstruction within 1e-10; ...'. Optionally, also record the winner's search-state objective (best[0]) in fit_unit and require it to equal objective(ft, w) within TOL_TERMS.

confirmed.title: C7 'laws hash verifies' is only a self-consistency check: no comparison with the registered laws_sha256, and verify_lock never checks documents_sha256
confirmed.file_line: lcr/fixtures.py:302 (load_laws), 1228, 1247-1250 (shard reload); lcr/lock.py:176-198 (verify_lock), 143 (documents_sha256 written, never read)
confirmed.rule_text: Registered C7: 'laws hash verifies, atoms rebuild from the explicit tables, ...'. FIXTURE_GATE_RULE.json binds laws_sha256 = 5c5e3bda...; the prompt says to freeze the complete fixture laws before any fixture algorithm runs.
confirmed.code_behaviour: load_laws only checks body['laws_sha256'] == laws_hash(body), a hash the JSON body carries for itself. It rebuilds atoms from the tables stored in that same JSON, not from the locked SPECS in fixtures.py. stage_fixture never compares the hash with FIXTURE_GATE_RULE.json['laws_sha256'] or with the lock's documents_sha256; it only records them. verify_lock checks code_files, deps, inputs and push status, but not documents_sha256, so a change to FIXTURE_LAWS.json is not caught at stage time. In shard mode, saved fix__* units are reloaded and combined without comparing their recorded laws_sha256 with the current laws.
confirmed.failure_scenario: After FIXTURE_LOCK, FIXTURE_LAWS.json is edited (say different sex_num or pair_counts), with atoms, properties and laws_sha256 recomputed consistently. Alternatively, a sharded run reuses fix__F3 results saved under a different laws file. load_laws, C7 (N == 4096, pairs <= 1e5, properties match) and verify_lock all pass, and FIXTURE_GATE.json reports GATE_MET under the registered gate on unregistered laws. Fix: refuse unless laws['laws_sha256'] == the rule's laws_sha256 == the lock's documents_sha256 entry, and check each reloaded unit's laws_sha256.

verdict.reason:
Each factual part of the claim checks out against the current code.

(1) lcr/fixtures.py:299-312 load_laws checks only that body['laws_sha256'] equals laws_hash(body). That hash is computed from the same JSON, so any edit that also recomputes the hash passes. It rebuilds atoms and properties from tables stored in that same file. It never calls build_laws()/SPECS and never compares with FIXTURE_GATE_RULE.json['laws_sha256'] (5c5e3bda...).

(2) In stage_fixture (lcr/fixtures.py:1263-1309), laws_sha256 and gate_rule_sha256 are only written into FIXTURE_GATE.json and never compared. The C7 check (~line 1016) tests only N == 4096, pairs <= 1e5 and law_properties(fam) == props. Both of those come from the loaded file.

(3) lcr/lock.py:143 writes documents_sha256, which includes FIXTURE_LAWS.json and FIXTURE_GATE_RULE.json. verify_lock (176-198) checks only code_files, deps, inputs and push status. GLOBS cover only .py files, so the laws and rule JSON are not locked files at all. That contradicts the lock docstring ("FIXTURE_LOCK: fixture laws, gate rule, ... -> fixture"). It also contradicts the prompt's binding requirements: "Freeze ... complete fixture laws and gate", "Push and verify each before the stage it governs" and "Push FIXTURE_LOCK before algorithms run on them".

(4) The shard reload (1288-1293) combines saved fix__* result.json files without reading the laws_sha256 in their record.json.

The independent verifier reads C7 as including the binding: replay_lcr.py check_fixture_laws computes both hash_ok and gate_rule_binds_same_laws. The stage's own C7 does not. So this is a real disagreement between the registered C7 text plus binding and the code, and by the study's own rule it is a defect.

Severity is lower than "verdict-changing". Under the registered, unchanged laws the computed verdict and route are correct. A false GATE_MET needs the laws file to differ from the registered one, or stale shard units saved under other laws. Either is a protocol violation, but one that the stage, as written, would accept without refusing. The external replay catches some of these cases: a laws-only edit (binding false) and most stale-unit cases (partition and arm mismatches). It does not catch a consistent edit of both the laws file and the rule's laws_sha256; only the unchecked documents_sha256 would reveal that.
verdict.suggested_fix:
Code, minimal:

(a) In stage_fixture, right after `laws = load_laws(laws_path)`, when laws_path is None (the registered path; the toy test passes its own laws_path and is unaffected), refuse unless all three match:
- `laws['laws_sha256'] == json.loads((PKG/'FIXTURE_GATE_RULE.json').read_text())['laws_sha256']`
- `_file_sha(PKG/'FIXTURE_LAWS.json')` equals the latest lock's `documents_sha256['FIXTURE_LAWS.json']`
- `_file_sha(PKG/'FIXTURE_GATE_RULE.json')` equals the latest lock's `documents_sha256['FIXTURE_GATE_RULE.json']`

Use lcr.lock.latest() to get the lock.

The alternative is to add to verify_lock, for stage == 'fixture' only, a check that those two documents match lock['documents_sha256']. Do not check every listed document: later SCIENCE documents may legitimately change while the fixture stage runs.

(b) In the shard reload (fixtures.py:1288-1293), include a saved fix__<id> unit only if `R.rec(f'fix__{id}')['laws_sha256'] == laws['laws_sha256']`. Otherwise refuse, or leave the set incomplete so the gate is GATE_NOT_MET / INCOMPLETE_FIXTURE_SET.

Text: reword C7 to "the laws' canonical hash verifies and equals the laws_sha256 bound in this rule and in FIXTURE_LOCK's documents_sha256; atoms rebuild from the explicit tables; ...".

confirmed.title: C1 and C5 enforce failure conditions that are not in the registered text
confirmed.rule_text: C1: tok/q MI identity 'for every D0 map and its D1 version ... for both decoders'. C5 lists the mapper terms, the decoder.json re-solve and the oracle terms within 1e-10 (TOL_TERMS); tolerances table has no 1e-9 C5 entry.
confirmed.code_behaviour: C1 also fails if any arm, mapper arms included, has |I(SEX;(tok,q)) - I(SEX;tok)| > 1e-15. C5 also fails with 'token_loss_helper:<x>' if decoder.token_losses totals differ from the row-level per_row sums by more than 1e-9, an absolute tolerance on totals that is not registered.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Both should pass by design. q is a function of the token, so the (tok, q) grouping equals the tok grouping and the MI is bitwise equal, and the helper error is about 1e-12 on totals of about 1e3. So neither should produce a spurious GATE_NOT_MET. Still, a CORRECTNESS_FAILURE:C5 could be triggered by a criterion that is not in the registered rule. Register both, or move them to descriptive diagnostics.

verdict.reason:
The claim holds. The code has two failure conditions that the registered text does not describe. I checked the current source; line numbers have moved by about 3 since the claim because of the concurrent C3 text edit.

(1) C1, lcr/fixtures.py:933-935. A second loop runs over every arm, mapper releases included, and appends `cid:tok_q` whenever |I(SEX;(tok,q)) - I(SEX;tok)| > 1e-15. The registered C1 text (gate_rule, around lines 397-399, and FIXTURE_GATE_RULE.json) limits the (token, q) test to "every D0 map and its D1 version ... for both decoders". Mapper arms (C-TASK, W-, K-) have no D0 partner in the bank, so the text does not cover them.

(2) C5, lcr/fixtures.py:1013-1015, with the value computed at 645. C5 also fails with `token_loss_helper:<x>` when lcr.decoder.token_losses totals on any exhaustive-oracle subset differ from the row-level dpc per_row sums by more than 1e-9 absolute. The C5 text lists only the mapper terms and the decoder.json re-solve, plus the oracle terms within TOL_TERMS = 1e-10. The tolerances table has no 1e-9 entry and the text never mentions the helper.

Neither condition can cause a spurious GATE_NOT_MET in practice:
- Mapper and D1 releases build q as dec.q[tok] (lcr/decoder.py encode_d1), so q is bitwise a function of the token. plugin_mi's np.unique over (tok, q) then groups the rows exactly as tok alone does, in the same order, so the two MI values are bitwise equal.
- token_losses and per_row both clip at 1e-12. The only difference is summation order: at most about log2(4096)·eps·1e5, roughly 1.5e-10, and realistically about 1e-12. That is below 1e-9.

So the verdict and route are unaffected. Still, the study prompt (line 135) treats any code/text disagreement as a defect to disclose and resolve, and a CORRECTNESS_FAILURE:C1 or :C5 could in principle cite a criterion that was never registered. This is the same kind of issue as the known C3 clarification. Severity: disclosure-only.
verdict.suggested_fix:
Change the text only and keep both checks. They fall under the prompt's mandatory items "token-preserving decoder changes leave full-token information unchanged" and "incremental MI/loss terms match independent reconstruction".

In gate_rule() (lcr/fixtures.py, around lines 397-411):
(a) Append to the C1 text: "; additionally every release of every arm (D0, D1 and mapper C-TASK / W- / K-) has I(SEX; (token, q)) == I(SEX; token) within 1e-15".
(b) Append to the C5 text: "; and the lcr.decoder.token_losses per-token totals (log loss and Brier) equal the row-level dpc.utility.per_row sums on every exhaustive-oracle subset within TOL_HELPER = 1e-9 absolute".
(c) Add a module constant TOL_HELPER = 1e-9 and list it under "tolerances". Use the constant at line 1014 instead of the literal 1e-9, and optionally a named TOL_TOKQ = 1e-15 at lines 929 and 934.

Then regenerate FIXTURE_GATE_RULE.json before the lock.

confirmed.title: C6 labels the 26 D1 fixed-map arms NOT_A_SEARCH, a label the registered text gives only to DIRECT-TASK and CLASS
confirmed.rule_text: C6: 'every arm carries EXHAUSTIVE_OPTIMAL ... or HEURISTIC with its gap'; own_problem_objectives: 'DIRECT-TASK, CLASS: not partition searches over the fine family (labelled NOT_A_SEARCH)'.
confirmed.code_behaviour: Every d1_fixed and d1_task arm (the 24 privacy maps plus FINE-TASK|D1, DIRECT-TASK|D1 and CLASS|D1) gets label NOT_A_SEARCH. The pass condition all(v['label']) holds for any non-empty string, so C6 cannot fail. That matches 'a heuristic gap is reported, not a failure'.
confirmed.failure_scenario: No verdict effect. The text says every arm is EXHAUSTIVE_OPTIMAL or HEURISTIC, but the result marks many arms NOT_A_SEARCH; add the D1 fixed-map arms to the NOT_A_SEARCH line of own_problem_objectives.

verdict.reason:
The claim holds, but it only affects what the text discloses. It does not change the verdict.

What the code does: in lcr/fixtures.py:1083-1085, label_arms gives the label NOT_A_SEARCH to every arm whose kind is d1_fixed or d1_task. Lines 900-903 set that kind for every `<D0 cid>|D1` arm made from the D0 bank. That bank comes from d0_bank (lines 705-760): FINE-TASK, CLASS, DIRECT-TASK, and the 24 privacy maps (4 PRIVACY families x 6 LAMS, which I checked by inspecting R.PRIVACY and F.LAMS). So 27 D1 control arms get NOT_A_SEARCH: 24 d1_fixed plus FINE-TASK|D1, DIRECT-TASK|D1 and CLASS|D1. The claim's title says 26; its body correctly says 24 + 3. The D0 DIRECT-TASK and CLASS arms also get NOT_A_SEARCH, through _own_value returning None (lines 1053-1054 and 1087-1088).

What the registered text says: C6 (lines 412-415) says "every arm carries EXHAUSTIVE_OPTIMAL ... or HEURISTIC with its gap". The only exception in own_problem_objectives (line 431, and FIXTURE_GATE_RULE.json:152) is "DIRECT-TASK, CLASS: ... labelled NOT_A_SEARCH". own_problem_objectives gives no entry at all for the D1 fixed-map controls. So the published result will label 27 arms in a way the registered text does not allow. For FINE-TASK|D1 and the 24 privacy D1 arms, a reader could reasonably expect a label against the D0 own-problem reference, because the partition is the same as the D0 arm's.

No verdict or route effect: C6 passes whenever every label is a non-empty string (line 1021), so it cannot fail. That matches "a heuristic gap is reported, not a failure". The labels are read only by the CSV writer (line 1211), not by trigger or gate_from_results.

The code matches the prompt's intent. The prompt says "optimizers are labelled heuristic when they differ from exhaustive references", and it describes bank B as "D1 versions of those EXACT fixed mappings: calibration-only controls, assignments unchanged". These are not optimizers, so NOT_A_SEARCH is correct. The registered text is what should change.
verdict.suggested_fix:
Change the text only, in gate_rule() in lcr/fixtures.py; the code stays as it is.

1. In own_problem_objectives (line 431), replace the "DIRECT-TASK, CLASS" entry with:
"D0 DIRECT-TASK, D0 CLASS": "not partition searches over the fine family (labelled NOT_A_SEARCH)",
"every <D0 config>|D1 control (the 24 d1_fixed privacy maps and FINE-TASK|D1, DIRECT-TASK|D1, CLASS|D1)": "the D0 assignments decoded by D1, not a search; labelled NOT_A_SEARCH (the matching D0 arm carries the search label)".

2. Change the C6 text to: "every searched arm (D0 FINE-TASK / privacy, C-TASK, W-, K-) carries EXHAUSTIVE_OPTIMAL (...) or HEURISTIC with its gap; D0 DIRECT-TASK / CLASS and every D1 fixed-map control carry NOT_A_SEARCH; a heuristic gap is reported, not a failure".

Then regenerate FIXTURE_GATE_RULE.json before the lock.

refuted.title: The T_star candidate set includes U|CLASS|i1o1|D1, whose I12 is exactly 0 in all four registered laws, so no fixture can trigger and GATE_NOT_MET is fixed before anything runs
refuted.reason:
The claim's facts are right, but the code is not wrong and does not disagree with the registered text. The registered text is also a faithful reading of the prompt, not a departure from it.

Facts confirmed:
- (1) The CLASS map is one token per predicted class. `R.parse_id('U|CLASS|i1o1|D1')` gives m1 = m2 = 1 and privacy_trained = False, so it sits in `TASK_ONLY_D1` (fixtures.py:324) and is never a privacy candidate in `trigger()` (around line 1131).
- (2) P(S=1 | c1, c2) = 1/2 in all four laws. In each family the clue (F1 confidence half, F2 j in {0,3}, F3/F4 bit b) is balanced within every class, so `plugin_mi` returns exactly 0.
- (3) Every canonical partition, including the all-merged one, is D1-budget-feasible in F2, F3 and F4 (FIXTURE_ORACLE_REPORT.md: 64/512, 64/64, 64/64). A hand check for F3/F4 agrees with a wide margin. Recipient 1: CLASS minus Bayes LL is about 0.0024 against a 0.005 budget; Brier excess is 2·(1/32)² ≈ 0.00195 against 0.003. Recipient 2: LL about 0.0029. F1 has 0 feasible recipient-2 partitions.

So the trigger cannot fire (`trigger()` lines 1118 and 1143) and GATE_NOT_MET / NO_FIXTURE_TRIGGERED is settled by the structure of the laws.

Why this is not a defect:
- (a) The code does exactly what FIXTURE_GATE_RULE.json registers. The claim says so itself.
- (b) Including CLASS matches the prompt. The binding sentence asks for the "strongest feasible task-only D1 compression". The prompt uses "task-only" to mean privacy-untrained: line 363 says "Fixed-map D1 privacy releases remain privacy-trained controls; do not relabel them task-only because the new decoder itself uses no SEX". CLASS-ONLY is privacy-untrained and is explicitly in the Adult T* (sec. 10, line 348).
- (c) The F3 purpose sentence is not contradicted. "task-only compression to 2 tokens per class merges along a and keeps the clue" describes the cap-2 task-objective map (C-TASK/FINE-TASK, exhaustive optimum at partitions [45, 45]). The gate rule never limits T_star to maps that use the full cap.
- (d) The GATE_NOT_MET is not false. If decisions alone, decoded by D1, meet both budgets with I12 = 0, then privacy-trained partitioning really adds nothing on these fixtures. Dropping CLASS would create a false GATE_MET: the gate would pass against a weaker baseline while the downstream claim A (P* vs T*, with CLASS-ONLY in T*) would be structurally unable to pass on the same law.

What the claim actually shows is a weakness in how the fixture bank was designed: the clue in F3/F4 is so weakly tied to the task that dropping it fits within budget. That is not a code/text disagreement. Changing the laws or the T_star set now, after role E's feasibility counts exist, would be the post-hoc favourable-example search the prompt forbids ("fixed finite bank; no unbounded hunt").

refuted.title: DECODER_ENABLED_ROUTE is assigned even when D1 enabled nothing (the D0 old map already qualifies)
refuted.reason:
This is not a disagreement between text and code, and it is not a bug that changes the verdict or the route. Code and registered text match exactly. FIXTURE_GATE_RULE.json (from lcr/fixtures.py:382-392) defines decoder_enabled as "Q_fm nonempty" and assignment_search_helps as "Q_new nonempty and (Q_fm empty or best_new <= best_fm - 0.01)". It sets ASSIGNMENT_SEARCH_ROUTE when helps holds on any triggered fixture and DECODER_ENABLED_ROUTE "otherwise". It lists d0_version_already_qualifies explicitly as a descriptive flag, not a route input. trigger() at lcr/fixtures.py:1144-1159 and gate_from_results() at 1180-1182 compute exactly that, and test_gate_truth_table and test_trigger_rule_cases lock that behaviour in.

The prompt's binding sentence (line 323) sets old-map against new-search: "only because D1 makes an old private map usable" leads to DECODER_ENABLED, and "If new assignment search also helps" leads to ASSIGNMENT_SEARCH. It defines only these two labels and asks for the rule to be frozen in advance. The registered rule meets that request: the case where the D0-decoded old map also qualifies is assigned to DECODER_ENABLED_ROUTE, and the D0 result is still recorded in the flag. The reviewer concedes that the registered parenthetical ("met by an OLD assignment decoded by D1 and new search adds < 0.01") is literally true in that case.

Nothing operational depends on the label either. GATE_MET or GATE_NOT_MET is computed before and separately from the route. The prompt's only consequence of DECODER_ENABLED_ROUTE, "include all calibration controls in Adult", is already satisfied regardless of route: lcr/run.py:118-120 code_ids() always includes d1_fixed_ids(). So a "wrong" label cannot change which Adult arms run, and cannot produce a false GATE_MET or a false GATE_NOT_MET. At most this is a reporting nuance, which the claim itself calls disclosure-only.

refuted.title: C2 never computes |q_D1 - q_D0| on the arms' D1 releases; the reported max_q_diff covers only the oracle's own subset solves
refuted.reason: The wording differs from the code, but the code checks the same thing, so no verdict can change. (1) C2 runs the q test (fixtures.py:938-944) on every block of every canonical partition, because recipient_oracle calls subset() on each block of each enumerated partition (fixtures.py:653-660). Every arm's partition must be one of those: _partition_index (fixtures.py:860-866, called in C5) raises AssertionError otherwise, which stops the run and produces no verdict at all, true or false. So every arm token is a checked subset. (2) The claim's failure case needs an arm's released q to come from a different path than the oracle's. No such path exists. The mapper builds its release.npz with dec.decode_policy and dec.release_arrays_d1 (mapper.py:1262-1265), exactly as d1_of does for the fixed-map D1 arms (fixtures.py:762-772). decode_policy solves with solve_batch on the integer label counts from the rows (the same integers as the oracle's bincount) and on pol.token_S. Its row results are bitwise equal to the oracle's solve_token (decoder.py:345-350). dpc.release.token_tables accumulates token_S from zeros in increasing fine-cell order (dpc/release.py:36-44), the same order the oracle uses to build S (blocks are filled over range(fine.F)). The fine tables are the same objects, or a to_dict round-trip of them for the mapper. The D0 vector is the same dpc.partition.smooth: qpc.kmeans.smooth is DPT.smooth (qpc/kmeans.py:68), and token_tables uses smooth(tS/tn, c). So each arm's per-token q_D1 and q_D0 are bitwise the oracle's q1 and q0 for that subset. A literal per-arm |q_D1 - q_D0| would give numbers already inside the reported max_q_diff, and C2 could not pass or fail differently. (3) The prompt's binding intent, 'calibrated-teacher null gives no population decoder improvement beyond numerical tolerance', is about losses. The code checks that loss condition for every canonical partition and for every D1 arm against its own D0 decoding. This is at most an optional wording clarification, not a disagreement that affects GATE_MET or GATE_NOT_MET.

refuted.title: The 'independent' loss and U recomputation calls the same dpc.utility.per_row the mapper uses, so the C3 U-equality check and the C5 deployed L/B checks cannot fail
refuted.reason:
The factual premise holds, but there is no disagreement between the text and the code, and nothing here can change the verdict or the route.

1) The premise checks out. Both sides call dpc.utility.per_row on the same data:
- U losses: lcr/fixtures.py:548-554 calls per_row(X["P"][i], X["y"][i], K). Problem.LU/BU at lcr/mapper.py:214-217 calls per_row(P[r], y[r], fine.K), with P = check_probs(T["p1"][tr]). Here T["p1"] is X["P"][1] (fixtures.py:489), tr = arange(N) (fixtures.py:491), and dpc/partition.py:47 check_probs only casts to float64 and validates.
- Deployed L/B: release_metrics (fixtures.py:527) and deployed_terms (mapper.py:956) both call per_row on the same release q and labels.
So the U check and the deployed L/B comparisons give a difference of exactly 0 when the plumbing is right.

2) The text does not claim separate loss code. measurements.independence says lcr.fixtures recomputes with "dpc.utility.per_row conventions for losses, its own plug-in MI". It names per_row for losses and only calls the MI "its own". The code does exactly this. L_i is registered as "mean true-label log loss, natural log, clip 1e-12", which matches per_row (CLIP = 1e-12, dpc/utility.py:35). "Mapper-reported values are only cross-checked" is also true. The comparisons still fail if the mapper's wiring diverges: a different row subset or order through tr, different labels through _yfit, a different K, a release.npz round trip that differs from the in-memory release, or the record storing the wrong field (for example limL in place of LU). So "cannot fail" overstates it. They are plumbing checks, which is what a check of reported against recomputed values is for.

3) The prompt's binding requirement is met by other paths. "Incremental MI/loss terms match independent reconstruction" refers to the search arithmetic. That is final_state_terms from lcr.decoder.token_losses token sums, and C5 compares it against the per_row row-level values: a different formula. C5 also compares every release against the exhaustive oracle, whose q comes from per-subset DC.solve_token on the fixture's own subset statistics, not from the mapper's decoder, and it checks token_loss_helper_diff. The "no runner imports" independence rule in the prompt (sections 3E and 14) governs the Stage-7 independent verifier, not lcr.fixtures.

4) Impact: the claim itself says the verdict and route are unaffected. A shared per_row convention error is not a gate bug either, because per_row is the registered definition of the loss.

This is redundancy in how strong the checks are, not a text/code disagreement or a bug that could give a false GATE_MET or GATE_NOT_MET.
